This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
Is it consistent that\[\omega_2\to (\alpha)_2^2\]for every $\alpha <\omega_2$?
#1170: [Va99,7.86]
set theory | 
ramsey theory
Laver [La82] proved the consistency of $\omega_2\to (\omega_12+1,\alpha)^2$ for all $\alpha<\omega_2$. Foreman and Hajnal [FoHa03] proved the consistency of $\omega_2\to (\omega_1^2+1,\alpha)^2$ for all $\alpha<\omega_2$.

 The partial consistency results listed assume substantial consistency strength. Laver's original result is relative to a huge cardinal. Foreman-Hajnal directly derives the partition relation from the combinatorial hypothesis CH + $\omega_1$ carries an $\omega_1$-dense ideal. The consistency strength of this hypothesis is established in Adolf-Sargsyan-Trang-Wilson-Zeman to be the same as $\text{ZF} + \text{AD}_{\mathbb{R}}+ \Theta$ is regular, and Theorem 6.26 of "Hod mice and the Mouse Set Conjecture" bounds that determinacy hypothesis by ZFC + a Woodin limit of Woodins. Note that the determinacy hypothesis is well above a proper class of Woodins, but that doesn't necessarily imply the problem itself requires large cardinal strength.
